commitSubject: dev script brought up to speed with promot-ready cutover

intentComments.note: package.json documents scripts with sibling `//<name>` string keys. `dev` has NO dedicated `//dev` key; the nearest documenting comments are the two group headers that bracket its steps.
intentComments.//generate-ts: Story 028 — generate TypeScript address interface (anvil only; mainnet-addresses.ts is hand-maintained, story 068)
intentComments.//serve-and-dev: Story 003 — API server + local dev orchestration
intentComments.observation: `dev` is the only entry key in this package.json carrying no `//<key>` doc comment of its own, despite being the local mirror of the entire promotion-ready cutover. Every mainnet key in the file has an extensive one.

base.command: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil & sleep 3 && npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve

variants.variantNote: CONFIRMED: there are no `dev:preview` / `dev:dry` / `dev:broadcast` keys. Unlike every mainnet entry point in this package.json (which all ship a PREVIEW_MODE=true sibling), the local mirror has no non-broadcasting variant. A closure/static audit cannot be corroborated by a preview run of this entry point; the only way to execute it is to broadcast against a local anvil.

shellParse.rawCommand: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil & sleep 3 && npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve
shellParse.operatorPrecedence: `&` binds looser than `&&`, so the shell splits the line into exactly TWO jobs at the `&`.

job1_background.command: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil
job1_background.failureSemantics: runs asynchronously; its exit status is NEVER checked by job 2. If clean:local fails, start:anvil never runs and job 2 proceeds anyway until forge fails to dial port 8545.

job2_foreground.command: sleep 3 && npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve
job2_foreground.failureSemantics: pure `&&` chain — any non-zero exit halts the remainder.

shellParse.noJobControlCleanup: Unlike the sibling keys `test:nft-flow` / `test:nudge-payout` / `test:balancer-donation`, which all end in `&& kill %1`, `dev` never kills the backgrounded anvil. It ends in the long-lived `npm run serve`, so anvil is intended to outlive the chain — but a failed chain also leaves an orphaned anvil holding port 8545, which the next `dev` run's `start:anvil` will collide with.

deletes: ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*  [OUTSIDE the repo — user's home Foundry state]
notes: Does NOT delete server/deployments/addresses.ts or local-addresses.ts, the two .ts artifacts the UI actually consumes. On an aborted run this leaves NO json and STALE TypeScript.
The `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` leg was added in this delta (commit 7d3862e, 'package.json anvil temp state cleanup step'). It reaches outside the repository into shared user state.
--host 0.0.0.0 binds all interfaces, not loopback — the dev chain is reachable from the local network.
--block-time 2 makes every transaction land in its own 2s block; this is what makes timestamp-dependent accrual real locally (cf. the --gas-estimate-multiplier note on step 3).
The ONLY anvil-readiness gate. No `cast block-number` poll. Failure mode is loud (forge cannot dial), so this is an availability nuisance rather than a correctness hazard.

steps.command: npm run clean:local && forge script script/DeployMocks.s.sol:DeployMocks --rpc-url http://localhost:8545 --broadcast --slow --gas-estimate-multiplier 300

flagNotes.--broadcast: This entry point DOES broadcast. It is safe only because --rpc-url is hardcoded to localhost:8545; there is no chain guard in the script itself (see chainGuard below).
flagNotes.--slow: one tx per block; mirrors the mainnet promotion-ready broadcast's --slow.
flagNotes.--gas-estimate-multiplier 300: 300% headroom. Mainnet promotion-ready:broadcast uses 200, documented as 'story 073's lesson: under --slow each transaction is a new block, so timestamp-dependent accrual does real SSTORE work the single-timestamp simulation pass never sees'. Local is set HIGHER than mainnet.
flagNotes.absent: No --skip-simulation (mainnet cutover uses it), no --legacy / --with-gas-price (mainnet cutover uses both), no --ledger.

reads: script/uniswap-artifacts/* (vm.getCode/vm.deployCode — canonical UniswapV2 + WETH9 creation bytecode)

chainGuard.detail: DeployMocks.s.sol contains NO `require(block.chainid == 31337)`. The only chainid reference is a `console.log("Chain ID:", block.chainid)` at line 365. The repo's own CLAUDE.md mandates that local relaxations 'must be gated behind an explicit block.chainid == 31337 branch'. Contrast script/interactions/AddressLoader.sol, which in this same delta ADDED exactly such a require.

steps.onChainEffect: cast send MockDola.mint(MockAutoDOLA, 2300e18) using the well-known anvil account-0 key — donates assets to the ERC4626 without minting shares, raising share price.
notes: set -e. Depends on jq, bc, cast.
Simulates yield for the DOLA/AutoDOLA leg ONLY. No USDC, no USDe, no sUSDS, no StableStaker, no NudgeStreamer time advance. The promotion-ready stack's new value flows are NOT exercised by this step.
No evm_increaseTime / anvil cheatcodes at all — pure cast calls.
Amount->wei is string concatenation ("${AMOUNT}000000000000000000"); a non-integer argument yields a malformed literal.

Both totalAssets() reads are `2>/dev/null`, so an RPC or code-less-address failure prints blank before/after and the script still reports 'Done!'. Combined with the progress-file-lies hazard, this is the chain's sharpest silent no-op.

steps.mapping: BY NAME from progressData.contracts (never positional CREATE matching against broadcast artifacts). Transforms: drop 0x0 checkpoint markers; strip leading `Mock`; drop DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES; drop UNISWAP_V2_BACKING_NAMES; re-key <Base>V2 -> <Base>.
notes: Does NOT read broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json. The fragile positional-CREATE pattern exists only in the mainnet scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-*.js family; the local path is on the safe by-name side.
Exits 1 if the progress file is absent, correctly halting the && chain.
CHANGED IN THIS DELTA (story-078): DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES grew from [NFTMigrator, BuggedPoolerV2Index6] to add DepositView, DepositPageView, MintPageView.

writes: server/deployments/addresses.ts  [git-tracked] — the ContractAddresses INTERFACE, written first
server/deployments/local-addresses.ts  [git-tracked] — `export const anvilAddresses: ContractAddresses`, written second
notes: Emits BOTH files. Hard-refuses chainId 1 with an explicit 'mainnet-addresses.ts is hand-maintained' message (story 068); any chainId other than 31337 exits 1.

CROSS-CHAIN COUPLING: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts imports ContractAddresses from ./addresses and annotates `mainnetAddresses: ContractAddresses`. So this LOCAL step rewrites the compile-time type contract the hand-maintained MAINNET address book is validated against.

endpoints: GET /            — static doc JSON incl. a hand-maintained (and badly drifted) availableContracts array
GET /health      — booleans for whether the two files loaded
GET /contracts   — flattens local.json contracts to {name: address}; 404 if local.json absent
notes: CORS wide open (cors() with no options).
Never terminates — this is the chain's terminal step, which is why anvil is deliberately left running.
No freshness check of any kind: /health reports deploymentsLoaded:true for a file from a previous run.
CHANGED IN THIS DELTA (story-078): 'DepositView' removed from the hardcoded availableContracts array.

jsChain.absent: No scripts/backup-*.js, no scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-*.js, no scripts/check-phlimbo-snapshot-age.js, no scripts/snapshot-*.js. The entire mainnet safety/snapshot preamble that guards promotion-ready:dry / :broadcast has no local counterpart — including the phlimbo-v2 staker snapshot that mainnet Phase 4e seeds MigratorV2V3 from.

orderingHazards.title: clean:local runs twice; the second run races LIVE anvil
orderingHazards.detail: `dev` invokes clean:local directly (background job 1), and deploy:local invokes it again ~3s later in the foreground — i.e. AFTER anvil is already up. That second run ends in `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`, which deletes the tmp working files of the RUNNING anvil rather than of a previous one. The first clean is the correctly ordered one; the second is both redundant and the hazardous one.

orderingHazards.title: progress.31337.json is written before broadcast and can lie
orderingHazards.detail: _writeProgressFile() is called inside run() after vm.stopBroadcast() but during forge's LOCAL execution pass, before any transaction is dispatched. package.json's own //promotion-ready:resume doc states this in the strongest terms for the mainnet keys ('after a crash IT LIES — it can name contracts that were never deployed'). The identical property holds locally. On abort the && chain stops, but the lying file SURVIVES on disk and is only removed at the start of the next deploy:local.

orderingHazards.title: simulate-yield.sh consumes a file, not the chain
orderingHazards.detail: It sources MockDola/MockAutoDOLA from progress.31337.json without any `cast code` probe. Composed with EH-02, a partially-broadcast deploy leaves it minting to a code-less address; `cast send` to an EOA-shaped target succeeds as a plain call, so the yield is silently not simulated while both totalAssets() reads (2>/dev/null) print blank and the script reports success.

orderingHazards.title: Non-atomic writes across three files that must agree
orderingHazards.detail: local.json, then addresses.ts, then local-addresses.ts are three separate writeFileSync calls across two processes, with no run-id or checksum tying them. A crash between them leaves addresses.ts describing run N while local-addresses.ts holds run N-1 — and because mainnet-addresses.ts is typed against addresses.ts, the skew propagates to the mainnet file's type check.

orderingHazards.title: clean:local does not delete the .ts outputs
orderingHazards.detail: It removes progress.31337.json and local.json but leaves addresses.ts and local-addresses.ts. On a chain that aborts after the clean you are left with NO json and STALE TypeScript — which reads as a successful prior deploy to the only consumers that matter (the UI repo; nothing inside this repo imports either file).

orderingHazards.title: A local anvil run rewrites the mainnet address book's type guard
orderingHazards.detail: addresses.ts is regenerated on every local run from anvil's local.json, and mainnet-addresses.ts is annotated against it. A contract present on mainnet but not _trackDeployment'ed in DeployMocks vanishes from the interface, silently un-typing the mainnet key; a purely local mock added to DeployMocks becomes a REQUIRED key on the mainnet object. The DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES / UNISWAP_V2_BACKING_NAMES denylists in extract-addresses.js exist solely to hold this line, and only a code comment enforces the lockstep.

orderingHazards.title: Background job's exit status is never checked
orderingHazards.detail: If clean:local fails in job 1, start:anvil never runs, yet job 2 sleeps 3 and proceeds regardless until forge fails to dial 8545.

orderingHazards.title: No `kill %1` — orphaned anvil on failure
orderingHazards.detail: The three sibling local-flow keys (test:nft-flow, test:nudge-payout, test:balancer-donation) all terminate with `&& kill %1`. `dev` does not, because serve is meant to be long-lived. A failed chain therefore leaves an orphaned anvil holding port 8545, which the next run's start:anvil collides with.

gitTrackedSideEffectsNote: All six are committed to the repository, so a single local `npm run dev` run dirties the working tree, and clean:local `rm`s two tracked files. The delta 3fb4e34..e1db0f1 contains exactly such a run (commits f29ecb0 'recent deploy of anvil', 3e0f1a5 'local run').
